new.headline: This week went to plan: all five runs were done at the planned distance, and the marathon-pace workout landed near goal pace. Next week builds to 44 miles with a 16-mile long run, and doubling to 80 miles is not the way to catch up.

answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer:
No, doubling to 80 miles would not work, and I would not do it. You ran about 40 miles this week, so 80 would double your load in one step, and twice-a-day running adds fatigue that easy days cannot repay. Your club mate's total is built over a long time and suits their own body, not yours.

You are not behind. The plan builds your volume steadily, and 44 miles next week is the right step. The long run is the key session, so put your effort there and keep the other easy days easy.

new.analysis:
This week went to plan. All five runs were done at the planned distance, 40 miles in total. The Wednesday workout held its marathon-pace miles between 8:30 and 8:40 per mile, which is the pace a 3:45 finish needs, and no time went into zone 4 or 5.

The one thing to correct is the long run, which was planned as easy with heart rate under 150. The average of 146 met that ceiling, but heart rate climbed from 143 to 149 and about half the run sat in zone 3. That is firmer than the label, and it adds fatigue to a run that should only build endurance.

| Session | Avg heart rate | Pace | Time in zone 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Easy runs (Tue, Thu, Sat) | 139 | 9:50/mi | 0% |
| Wednesday workout | 150 | 9:04/mi | 72% |
| Long run | 146 | 9:59/mi | 55% |

A share in the 60s is expected on a week with two hard sessions, but this week had only one, so the gap came mainly from the long run. Your easy share was 64 percent against the 80 percent goal.

Your miles have moved quickly: 37 two weeks back, 53 the week before when you ran past the plan, and 40 this week. The 53-mile week came with a 20-mile long run, so this week's 40 was a sensible step back. Next week's 44 miles is about a 10 percent rise, a steady pace of growth for this build.

The long run stays the key session, so it grows to 16 miles with three of those at marathon pace. Thursday's 8 miles is the mid-week medium-long run, easy enough to follow Wednesday's workout without strain. Wednesday moves to threshold reps, which the build phase adds, so marathon pace is practiced mainly on Sunday.

Nothing in your check-in points to a problem: pain stayed at zero, sleep averaged 7 hours, and stress was normal. That supports the steady build and gives no reason to add running on top of the plan.
